history.idea: Replace the random shuffle with a target-similarity filter. In select(): (1) drop exact duplicates by hashing the stripped text; (2) drop docs whose alphabetic-character fraction is below 0.7, or that look like spam (e.g. contain "Click here", "coupon", "discount code", "free shipping"); (3) fit sklearn TfidfVectorizer(sublinear_tf=True, min_df=2, stop_words="english") on target_sample plus the surviving docs, and score each doc by cosine similarity to the mean target_sample vector; (4) sort docs by score descending, with ties broken by the seeded RNG from CURATE_SEED; (5) walk the sorted list, accumulating an approximate token count (len(text)/4 per doc), and stop once it reaches T, so the returned list covers about T tokens with no cycling needed. Use the same seeded order as the fallback if fewer than T tokens survive.
history.outcome: dev 1.9533 against 1.9583 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Keep the seeded random shuffle as the final order, but first remove near-duplicates and junk. (a) Drop docs whose alphabetic-character fraction is below 0.7 or that contain spam phrases ("Click here", "coupon", "discount code", "free shipping", "order ... online"). (b) Near-duplicate removal: build word 5-gram shingle sets per doc, compute MinHash with 64 seeded hash permutations, use LSH banding (16 bands of 4 rows) to find candidate pairs, and keep a doc only if its estimated Jaccard with every already-kept doc is below 0.5. Process candidates in the seeded shuffle order so the kept doc is random. (c) Return the shuffled survivors; if they total fewer than T tokens, cycle them as the trainer already does. Do not use target similarity or truncate to T tokens.
history.outcome: dev 1.9960 against 1.9583 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: In select(), replace the cosine-to-mean-centroid score with a domain classifier score, and drop the alphabetic-fraction and spam-phrase rules. Fit sklearn TfidfVectorizer(sublinear_tf=True, min_df=2, stop_words="english") on target_sample plus all docs. Train LogisticRegression(C=1.0, class_weight="balanced", max_iter=1000) with the 200 target_sample docs as positives and a seeded random sample of 200 pool docs as negatives. Score every pool doc with predict_proba for the positive class; for pool docs that were sampled as negatives, use 5-fold cross-fitted predictions so they are not scored by a model that saw them. Order docs by score descending, breaking ties with random.Random(int(os.environ.get("CURATE_SEED", 0))). Exact-duplicate removal by hashing the stripped text stays. Walk the sorted list, accumulating len(text)/4 per doc, and stop once the total reaches T, as in experiment 1. Use the seeded shuffle as the fallback if fewer than T tokens survive.
history.outcome: dev 1.9847 against 1.9583 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Keep the baseline seeded random shuffle as the final order, but drop only damaged/scrambled docs using a vocabulary-coverage test instead of the alphabetic-fraction rule. In select(): (1) exact-dedupe by hashing the stripped text (as in experiment 1). (2) Build a vocabulary set = lowercased alphabetic words that appear in target_sample, plus words whose document frequency across the pool is at least 20. (3) For each doc, compute the fraction of its alphabetic word tokens (lowercased, regex [A-Za-z]+) that are in the vocabulary; drop the doc if the fraction is below 0.6 or it has fewer than 5 words. Do not apply the alpha-fraction threshold or spam-phrase rules. (4) Return the seeded shuffle of the survivors, with no truncation, so the trainer reads them front to back and cycles only if needed.
history.outcome: dev 1.9470 against 1.9583 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Keep the current best pipeline (exact dedupe, vocabulary-coverage filter, seeded shuffle, no truncation) and add a format-match filter. For each doc, compute its "wiki-style token ratio": the fraction of whitespace-separated tokens that are standalone punctuation or markers (e.g. ",", ".", "(", ")", ";", ":", "@-@", "@.@", "@,@", "=" headers). Compute the median of this ratio over target_sample, and drop any pool doc whose ratio is below 0.5 times that median. Leave the vocabulary-coverage rule and the seeded shuffle order unchanged, and do not truncate.
